name: La Mar
note: Gastón Acurio's flagship cebichería. Lunch only, no reservations — get the ceviche tasting.
address: Av. Mariscal La Mar 770, Miraflores, Lima

name: Isolina
note: Nostalgic Limeño tavern, huge sharing plates: ceviche with fried octopus, arroz con pato. Reserve.
address: Av. San Martín 101, Barranco, Lima

name: Canta Rana
note: Beloved, cash-only, 17 kinds of ceviche, football-and-clippings decor. Expect a line.
address: Génova 101, Barranco, Lima

name: Barra Maretazo
note: Casual, beachy cevichería; shrimp risotto and very fresh fish. Second branch at Calle Berlín 340, also Miraflores.
address: Calle Alcanfores 373, Miraflores, Lima

name: Grimanesa Vargas Anticuchos
note: Peru's most famous anticuchera; beef-heart skewers in panca-chile marinade. Evenings, cash, go early.
address: Calle Ignacio Merino 466, Miraflores, Lima

name: La Lucha Sanguchería
note: Modern sandwich classic; chicharrón sandwich + huayro fries + lucuma juice.
address: Parque Kennedy, Miraflores, Lima

name: El Chinito
note: Historic chicharrón sandwich shop, repeatedly voted Lima's best. Cash only.

name: Picarones Mary
note: Syrup-drenched squash/sweet-potato doughnuts from a Parque Kennedy cart. A must-try.

name: Mayta
note: Jaime Pesaque's tasting menu; No. 39 on World's 50 Best 2025; coast, Andes & Amazon in 10 courses. Reserve.
address: Av. Mariscal La Mar 1285, Miraflores, Lima

name: Central / Kjolle
note: If a slot opens: Virgilio Martínez's ecosystem tasting menu, often World's No. 1. Kjolle is its sister next door.
address: Av. Pedro de Osma 301, Barranco, Lima

name: Lady Bee
note: BOOKED the 16th. Peru's top bar, World's 50 Best. Produce-driven cocktails + small plates.
address: Av. Pedro de Osma 205, Barranco, Lima

name: Carnaval
note: The other 50-Best bar; ask for the 'Gran Carnaval' flight; famous ice program. Reserve.
address: Av. Pardo y Aliaga 662, San Isidro, Lima

name: Tostaduría Bisetti
note: Pioneering roaster + coffee lab. Try the 'Brew Fruit' (cold coffee + pineapple).
address: Av. Pedro de Osma 116, Barranco, Lima

name: BarBarian
note: Craft-beer taproom, 20+ Peruvian taps. Laid-back.
address: Av. Pedro de Osma 144, Barranco, Lima

name: Bajada de Baños & Pasaje Oroya
note: Mural epicentre; look for Jade Rivera & Yandy Graffer works near the Bridge of Sighs.

name: Dédalo
note: 30-year institution in a restored mansion: 700+ artists across themed rooms, courtyard café.
address: Jirón Sáenz Peña 295, Barranco, Lima

name: Museo Pedro de Osma
note: Colonial art in a gorgeous mansion with stunning stained glass.
address: Av. Pedro de Osma 421, Barranco, Lima

name: Faster Skateshop
note: Core shop since 2004 (Baker, Deathwish, Independent, Thrasher). In the Multicentro gallery basement.
address: Av. Larco 345, Miraflores, Lima

name: Freeway Skateshop
note: Specialists since 1995; decks plus scooters/blades. Mon–Sat 11–8.
address: Grimaldo del Solar 142, Miraflores, Lima

name: Skate Outlet
note: Oldest/most complete shop in Peru (since 1998); Baker, Plan B, Real, Antihero.
address: Av. Aviación 5092, C.C. Santa Rosa, Tienda 4, Higuereta, Surco, Lima

name: Dunkelvolk
note: Peruvian skate/surf apparel brand (est. 1996); good streetwear souvenir hunt.

name: Museo Larco
note: One of the world's great museums; pre-Columbian gold, ceramics, the famous erotic gallery.
address: Av. Simón Bolívar 1515, Pueblo Libre, Lima

name: San Francisco Catacombs
note: Underground ossuary beneath a Baroque monastery; used as a cemetery until 1810. Guided only.

name: Casa Aliaga
note: Viceregal mansion gifted by Pizarro, still owned by the same family 480+ years on. By tour.
address: Jirón de la Unión 224, Lima

name: Magic Water Circuit
note: Choreographed illuminated fountains at night; kitschy, huge, genuinely fun.

name: Pachapapa
note: Open-air courtyard with a clay oven on Plazoleta San Blas; roast dishes, cuy for the brave.

name: La Cusqueñísima
note: Family picantería since 1986, ~20 min from centre; baked cuy, choclo con queso, sarzas.

name: Cicciolina
note: Creative Andean-Mediterranean on the second floor of a restored colonial mansion; Cusco's enduring favourite. Reserve.
address: Calle Palacio 110, 2nd floor, Cusco

name: Green Point
note: Cusco's best-known vegan spot; even for omnivores, a great-value tasting lunch.

name: San Blas artisan quarter
note: Casa Mérida ceramics, Mendívil figures, the 7 Angelitos alley; the artist heart of Cusco.
address: Plazoleta San Blas, Cusco

name: Twelve-Angled Stone
note: Famous perfectly-fitted Inca stone in an old palace wall; a two-minute marvel.

name: Qorikancha
note: The Inca Temple of the Sun beneath Santo Domingo church; small site museum attached.

name: Skatepark La Florida
note: Basic free concrete park; the spot to meet local skaters/fingerboarders. Community is social-media-run; ask around.

name: Mil
note: Virgilio Martínez's high-altitude tasting menu beside the Moray terraces. A destination in itself — book far ahead.

name: Chuncho
note: Andean techniques on Andean ingredients; roast lamb, cuy, chicha, simply plated.

name: Moray
note: Concentric circular Inca terraces; an agricultural 'laboratory' of microclimates.

name: Pisac Market & Ruins
note: Hilltop ruins with a solar observatory, plus one of the valley's best craft markets.

name: Indio Feliz
note: The town's most-loved spot; colourful French-Peruvian; a rewarding post-hike dinner.

name: Café de París
note: French-owned patisserie; best bread/pastries in town and box lunches for the mountain.

name: Town Food Market
note: Cheapest eats in town; set menus from ~8 soles. Try fresh Andean trout.

name: Taquile Island
note: UNESCO-listed for textiles woven by the men; peaceful, car-free, fresh-trout lunch.

name: Sillustani
note: Pre-Inca Qolla funerary towers (chullpas) on a peninsula; magic at golden hour.

name: Puno Cathedral
note: Andean-Baroque façade on the main plaza; a quick, striking stop.

name: Yavarí Steamship
note: A 160-year-old British-built iron steamship, now a floating museum. Delightfully odd.

name: Cochahuasi Animal Sanctuary
note: Family-run rescue for Andean condors, spectacled (Andean) bears, pumas, macaws and vicuñas; the ticket funds the release program. Ethical, and right on the way to Pisac.
address: Cochahuasi Animal Sanctuary, Km 22 Cusco–Pisac road, Cusco

name: Awana Kancha
note: “Living museum” of llamas, alpacas, vicuñas and guanacos you can feed, plus live weaving demonstrations. Quick stop; pairs with Cochahuasi.

name: Islas Palomino
note: Boat tour out to a wild sea-lion colony you can swim with; seabirds and penguins too. Half-day.

name: Pantanos de Villa
note: Protected coastal wetland with ~200 bird species, flamingos among them. Easy half-day.

name: Inkaterra Machu Picchu Pueblo
note: Spectacled-bear rescue project and cloud-forest birding on the hotel grounds.

name: Mandor Gardens
note: Birding and a waterfall walk, straight out of town.

name: MALI – Museo de Arte de Lima
note: The city's main fine-art museum, pre-Columbian through contemporary.

name: Museo Amano
note: Exquisite Chancay textiles; small, timed entry.

name: MAC Lima
note: Contemporary art; pairs with the Barranco street-art walk.

name: Museo de Arte Precolombino / MAP
note: Larco's sister collection — gold, silver, ceramics — in a gorgeous mansion, with MAP Café, one of Cusco's best restaurants, out in the courtyard.
address: Museo de Arte Precolombino, Plazoleta Nazarenas 231, Cusco

name: Museo Machupicchu / Casa Concha
note: The artifacts Bingham took to Yale, now returned — the context you don't get at the site itself.

name: La Candelaria
note: Afro-Peruvian and criollo peña with live music and dance; a good Friday night out.
